notes_for_editor: Corpus covers Light-House Board reports only from 1891 and the Life-Saving reports to 1909; the 1850s-1880s are therefore from LighthouseFriends (secondary, summarized) and the USLHS roster. Abyssinia date: the master's letter is dated 9 Nov 1900 and says the crew came 'last night', so 8 Nov. The Gettysburg story for Peter Bird is family lore as retold by LighthouseFriends and is labelled so; the Cyclorama claim was deliberately left out. The 1898 newspaper's 'Will Rohrig of the lighthouse force' was not linked to the roster's William Rohrig in the text. The 1938 Bulletin passage on ice was too column-interleaved to quote; only the 1936-39 index entry is used and the year of the ice event is unknown. Roster dates from the USLHS page; record height 13.5 m not confirmed (USLHS gives 38 ft base to centre of lantern; Wikipedia 44 ft). Bennetts efficiency flag: year unknown (index volume 1912-17). The Eagle Harbor Lifesaving Station (separate record us-mi-eagle-harbor-coast-guard-station-boathouse) is not covered here. Fact-check 2026-10-27: steamer name corrected from 'Thomas Maitland' (a misreading of the garbled Bulletin OCR) to Thomas Maytham, confirmed from WMHS (source 17). KCHS and LighthouseFriends disagree on 1850/1851 and on when the Fresnel lens came; stated in the text.
